name: Slice
q: How do I fix my slice?
intro: The ball curves hard to the right (for right-handers), usually from a clubface that is open to the swing path.

name: Hook
q: How do I stop hooking the ball?
intro: The ball curves hard left. Usually a closed clubface relative to the path, often from an over-active release or a strong grip.

name: Shanks
q: How do I stop shanking?
intro: The ball comes off the hosel and shoots right. Often caused by moving toward the ball in the downswing or an open face with the handle too far out.

name: Fat & thin shots
q: How do I stop hitting it fat or thin?
intro: Hitting the ground before the ball, or catching it too high on the face. Mostly a low-point and weight-shift problem.

name: Topping the ball
q: Why do I keep topping the ball?
intro: The leading edge hits the top half of the ball. Often from standing up, early extension or a scooping release.

name: Iron contact
q: How do I hit my irons more solidly?
intro: Ball-first contact with a forward-leaning shaft. The difference between flushed irons and weak, high shots.

name: Early extension
q: How do I fix early extension?
intro: Hips move toward the ball in the downswing and you lose your posture. One of the most common faults among amateurs.

name: Over the top
q: How do I stop coming over the top?
intro: The club moves outward at the start of the downswing and cuts across the ball. The classic source of pulls and slices.

name: Casting & lag
q: How do I stop casting and create lag?
intro: Releasing the wrist angle too early from the top. Costs speed and leads to scooping and thin shots.

name: Sway & weight shift
q: How do I shift my weight properly?
intro: Sliding off the ball in the backswing or hanging back in the downswing instead of rotating and moving pressure forward.

name: Takeaway & backswing
q: What does a good takeaway and backswing look like?
intro: The first move sets everything up: club path, face, width and turn.

name: Transition & downswing
q: How should I start the downswing?
intro: Sequencing from the top: what moves first and how the club drops into the slot.

name: Hip rotation
q: How do I rotate my hips properly?
intro: How the lower body turns and clears so the arms and club can swing through.

name: Release & clubface control
q: How do I square the clubface at impact?
intro: How the face rotates through impact. The biggest factor for where the ball starts.

name: Grip
q: How should I grip the golf club?
intro: Hand position and pressure. A small change here changes face control more than almost anything else.

name: Setup & posture
q: What is the correct golf setup and posture?
intro: Stance, ball position, spine angle and alignment before the club ever moves.

name: Driver & distance
q: How do I hit my driver longer and straighter?
intro: Launch, attack angle, tee height and the setup changes that make the driver different from irons.

name: Wedges & pitching
q: How do I hit better pitch shots?
intro: Partial wedge shots and distance control from 30 to 100 yards.

name: Chipping
q: How do I chip better?
intro: Short shots around the green: technique, club choice and the yips.

name: Bunker shots
q: How do I get out of the bunker?
intro: Greenside sand shots: using the bounce and hitting the sand, not the ball.

name: Putting
q: How do I putt better?
intro: Stroke, speed control and reading greens.

name: Speed training
q: How do I increase my swing speed?
intro: Overspeed training and protocols to swing faster.

name: Mobility & fitness
q: Which exercises help my golf swing?
intro: Flexibility and strength that make the positions possible in the first place.

name: How to practice
q: How should I practice golf?
intro: Structuring range sessions, drills and feedback so practice actually transfers to the course.

name: Course management
q: How do I score better without changing my swing?
intro: Target selection, club choice and strategy.

name: Mental game
q: How do I improve my mental game?
intro: Routines, pressure and staying out of your own way.

name: Swing fundamentals
q: What are the fundamentals of the golf swing?
intro: Overall swing concepts and models that tie the pieces together.
